title: Graph neural network modeling of pedestrian space vitality in campus waterfront space: a Flow-Dwell perspective for design translation.
summary: A graph neural network links contextual pedestrian-flow and dwell patterns across 42 spatial units on two campuses to measured waterfront-space vitality, outperforming the reported conventional baselines; the design translation remains a two-campus result.
ai_technology: GNN message passing models contextual links among 42 pedestrian-space units using Wi-Fi probe-derived Flow/Dwell and spatial attributes.

evidence.unknown: Comparison against conventional models supports the reported predictive gain; the paper has no out-of-campus replication and the two-campus scope is retained.
